Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1256 AM CDT Tue Aug 04 2026

Valid 051200Z - 061200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM MISSOURI
INTO ILLINOIS...OVER NORTHEAST NEW MEXICO INTO THE TEXAS
PANHANDLE...AND OVER SOUTHEAST ARIZONA...

...SUMMARY...
Isolated severe storms appear possible from Missouri into central
Illinois, over portions of southeast Arizona, and from northeast New
Mexico into the Oklahoma/Texas Panhandles Wednesday afternoon and
evening.

...MO...southern IA...central IL...
A shortwave trough will move across the Upper Midwest to Great Lakes
on Wednesday, with a weak surface trough roughly from northern MI
southwestward into northern MO. A plume of upper 60s to low 70s F
dewpoints will exist from MO into IA and IL, supporting around 1500
J/kg MUCAPE. This, combined with around 35 kt deep shear should
support scattered strong to severe storms with mixed mode. Locally
damaging wind gusts are most likely as storms congeal and produce
outflow. A few of the initial cells may produce marginal hail.

...Northeast NM into the OK/TX Panhandles...
Storms should form over the high terrain of northeast NM after 20Z
with a modest northwest flow regime aloft. High pressure will exist
over the central Plains, but surface winds will back to easterly and
provide moisture into the region late in the day. Strong heating and
steep low-level lapse rates will foster strong wind gusts.

...Southeast AZ...
Westerly surface winds with 50s to near 60 F dewpoints and daytime
heating will support storms over the eastern Mogollon Rim / White
Mtns, with some west/southwest propagation possible. MUCAPE should
rise to at least 1500 J/kg, with PWAT near 1.25" supporting locally
strong wind gusts.

..Jewell.. 08/04/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0221 PM CDT Mon Aug 03 2026

Valid 051200Z - 061200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM EASTERN 
KANSAS INTO WEST-CENTRAL ILLINOIS...OVER PORTIONS OF SOUTHERN 
ARIZONA...AND FROM NORTHEAST NEW MEXICO INTO THE OKLAHOMA/TEXAS
PANHANDLES......

...SUMMARY...
Isolated severe storms appear possible from eastern Kansas into
west-central Illinois, over portions of southern Arizona, and from 
northeast New Mexico into the Oklahoma/Texas Panhandles Wednesday
afternoon and evening.

...Synopsis...
Broadly cyclonic flow will remain across the north-central US on
D3/Wednesday, with an embedded short-wave trough and associated
mid-level jet streak moving through the mid and lower MO Valley. At
the surface, a cold front will extend from the Great Lakes back
westward into the Mid-Missouri Valley and south and west into the
southern Great Plains.

...Lower Missouri/mid Mississippi Valleys into eastern Kansas...
Elevated storms are likely to be ongoing at the start of the D3
period across portions of NE and IA into southern WI and northern
IL. The evolution of this convection and resulting outflows will
likely have impacts on placement of the front by the afternoon. This
leads to some uncertainty in where the best corridor will be for
renewed storm development by the afternoon. Nonetheless, guidance
suggests that a corridor of moderate to strong instability will
develop across portions of central Missouri/eastern Kansas. The
strongest shear remains mainly parallel to and along and north of
the cold front. Lapse rate profiles across central/northern Missouri
are poor, but a more favorable convection free air mass with steep
low to mid-level lapse rates will exist further south of the front
into south-central/southern Missouri and across eastern Kansas. This
narrow region of more favorable overlap of shear/instability/lapse
rates may support isolated supercell development and potential for
large hail, damaging winds, and perhaps a tornado.

...Southern Arizona...
Convection will build again across the high terrain in southern
Arizona D3/Wednesday before dropping southward into the lower
deserts. While deep-layer shear will remain relatively weak, the
presence of a deep, well-mixed boundary layer will support the
potential for isolated severe wind gusts during the afternoon into
evening.

...Northeast New Mexico into the Oklahoma/Texas Panhandles...
Convective development is expected across the Sangre de Cristo
Mountains and adjacent Raton Mesa Wednesday afternoon. Guidance
suggests convection may also develop to the east across the OK/TX
Panhandles, with potential for convection to grow upscale and
potentially move across the Texas Panhandle and collide with
convection out of eastern New Mexico. Given the hot/dry/well mixed
air mass to the south of the front, this may pose a conditional risk
for strong to severe wind and expansion of the 5% area was
warranted.

..Thornton.. 08/03/2026

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0329 AM CDT Mon Aug 03 2026

Valid 061200Z - 111200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Day 4/Thursday...

Broad troughing is forecast from the northern Plains through the
Great Lakes with a series of disturbances moving through that
airflow pattern. Elsewhere, an elongated vorticity ribbon will
progress from the central and southern Appalachians into the
Northeast. At the surface, a front initially from the southern Great
Lakes into the southern Plains is forecast to weaken. Over the
eastern CONUS, southerly winds will maintain a broad corridor of 70+
F dewpoints along and east of the Appalachians, which will
contribute to moderate instability by afternoon. Aided by the
approach of the disturbance aloft, thunderstorms are expected to
increase in coverage through the afternoon with some severe weather
possible. Generally weak vertical shear and the absence of a
coherent front in the region lead to uncertainty in where the
greatest threat may materialize.

An isolated severe threat may also develop along the front from the
Ozark Plateau into the southern High Plains, and in AZ during the
afternoon and evening.  
 

...Day 5/Friday...

An intense mid/upper-level low is expected to evolve over central
Canada with upper highs situated over the Great Basin and off the
Mid-Atlantic Coast. Between those features, corridors of stronger
mid-level flow are forecast from the northern Rockies into the
northern Plains, and to a lesser extent over the Northeast.
Some severe weather threat may again materialize from the
Mid-Atlantic into southern New England in the vicinity of a surface
trough. However, the strongest vertical shear is forecast to be
displaced to the north of the stronger instability, leading to
uncertainty in the extent of the severe weather threat. Isolated
severe storms also appear possible along a front moving into the
upper MS Valley.


...Days 6-8/Saturday through Monday...

The various 00Z ensemble means indicate an upper low initially over
Hudson Bay shifting east into northern QC with persistent ridging
over the southern CONUS. Between those features, a belt of enhanced
mid-level flow is forecast across the northern tier of states with
some signal for continued troughing through Sunday over the Great
Lakes into the OH Valley. At the surface, there is ensemble member
clustering in surface low positions over the northern Plains along a
front extending into the upper Great Lakes. There is a model signal
for the front to continue into the Great Lakes and Midwest, where
some severe weather threat appears possible. A separate severe
weather risk may also persist from the Mid-Atlantic into New
England.

..Mead.. 08/03/2026

1247 AM CDT Tue Aug 04 2026

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE SOUTHERN ROCKIES...SOUTHEAST ARIZONA AND IN THE WESTERN
CAROLINAS...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts and hail will be possible from
late afternoon into mid evening in parts of southern Rockies and
southeast Arizona. Severe gusts will also be possible in parts of
the western Carolinas.

...Southern Rockies...
A pocket of moderate instability will develop today across the
southern Rockies. As surface temperatures warm, convection will
initiate in the higher terrain of the Sangre de Cristos by
afternoon. Thunderstorms will develop and move east-southeastward
into the lower elevations of northeast New Mexico and southeast
Colorado. The instability combined with steep low to mid-level lapse
rates will support isolated severe wind gusts and hail.

...Southeast Arizona...
An axis of moderate instability will develop this afternoon in
southeast Arizona. MLCAPE is forecast to peak in the 1000 to 1500
J/kg range by late afternoon with thunderstorms developing near the
instability axis. The storms will move west-southwestward across
southeast Arizona from late afternoon into the early to mid evening.
The instability along with steep low to mid-level lapse rates will
support isolated severe wind gusts.

...Western Carolinas...
A mid-level low will remain over northern Georgia today. To the east
of the low, an axis of moderate instability is forecast to develop
over the western Carolinas by afternoon. Warming surface
temperatures in the higher terrain will result in scattered
convective initiation across the southern Appalachians. As
instability peaks and low-level lapse rates become steep in the
afternoon, an isolated wind-damage threat is expected to develop in
the western Carolinas.

..Broyles/Supinie.. 08/04/2026
